D000482.s: An extra-embryonic membranous sac derived from the yolk sac of reptiles; birds; and mammals. It lies between two other extra-embryonic membranes, the amnion and the chorion. The allantois serves to store urinary wastes and mediate exchange of gas and nutrients for the developing embryo.

D000860.s: Sub-optimal oxygen levels in the ambient air of living organisms.

D001113.s: Education centers authorized by the Comprehensive Health Manpower Training Act, 1971, for the training of health personnel in areas where health needs are the greatest. May be used for centers other than those established by the United States act.

D003223.s: A republic in central Africa lying between gabon and democratic republic of the congo and south of Cameroon. Its capital is Brazzaville.

D003616.s: A congenital abnormality of the central nervous system marked by failure of the midline structures of the cerebellum to develop, dilation of the fourth ventricle, and upward displacement of the transverse sinuses, tentorium, and torcula.

D006080.s: An oocyte-containing structure in the cortex of the ovary. The oocyte is enclosed by a layer of granulosa cells providing a nourishing microenvironment (follicular fluid). The number and size of follicles vary depending on the age and reproductive state of the female.

D006611.s: Respiratory support system used primarily with rates of about 100 to 200/min with volumes of from about one to three times predicted anatomic dead space. Used to treat respiratory failure and maintain ventilation under severe circumstances.

D006765.s: Hospitals which provide care to the patient for the period following an acute illness until health is restored.

D006970.s: Disorders characterized by hypersomnolence during normal waking hours that may impair cognitive functioning.

D007120.s: Field of chemistry that pertains to immunological phenomena and the study of chemical reactions related to antigen stimulation of tissues. It includes physicochemical interactions between antigens and antibodies.

D007195.s: Numerous islands in the Indian Ocean situated east of Madagascar, north to the Arabian Sea and east to Sri Lanka.

D010249.s: Inflammation of the parametrium, the connective tissue of the pelvic floor, extending from the subserous coat of the uterus laterally between the layers of the broad ligament.

D010304.s: An inflammatory reaction involving the folds of the skin surrounding the fingernail. It is characterized by acute or chronic purulent, tender, and painful swellings of the tissues around the nail, caused by an abscess of the nail fold.

D010515.s: Any restorative and replacement device that is used as a therapeutic aid in the treatment of periodontal disease. It is an adjunct to other forms of periodontal therapy and does not cure periodontal disease by itself. (Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 3d ed)

D010788.s: The synthesis by organisms of organic chemical compounds, especially carbohydrates, from carbon dioxide using energy obtained from light rather than from the oxidation of chemical compounds. Photosynthesis comprises two separate processes: the light reactions and the dark reactions.

D010821.s: Those physicians who have completed the education requirements specified by the American Academy of Family Physicians.

D010968.s: Materials incorporated mechanically in plastics (usually PVC) to increase flexibility, workability or distensibility; due to the non-chemical inclusion, plasticizers leach out from the plastic and are found in body fluids and the general environment.

D011905.s: Family of retrovirus-associated DNA sequences (ras) originally isolated from Harvey (H-ras, Ha-ras, rasH) and Kirsten (K-ras, Ki-ras, rasK) murine sarcoma viruses.

D012773.s: A type of shock that occurs as a result of a surgical procedure.

D013789.s: A group of hereditary hemolytic anemias in which there is decreased synthesis of one or more hemoglobin polypeptide chains. There are several genetic types with clinical pictures ranging from barely detectable hematologic abnormality to severe and fatal anemia.

D014201.s: Infections caused by infestation with worms of the class Trematoda.

D014458.s: Fractures of the larger bone of the forearm.

D014890.s: A multisystemic disease of a complex genetic background. It is characterized by inflammation of the blood vessels (vasculitis) leading to damage in any number of organs. The common features include granulomatous inflammation of the respiratory tract and kidneys.

D014951.s: Penetrating wounds caused by a pointed object.

D015259.s: Any drugs that are used for their effects on dopamine receptors, on the life cycle of dopamine, or on the survival of dopaminergic neurons.

D016131.s: A classification of lymphocytes based on structurally or functionally different populations of cells.

D017288.s: Amount of stimulation required before the sensation of pain is experienced.

D017381.s: Organelles in which the splicing and excision reactions that remove introns from precursor messenger RNA molecules occur.

D017604.s: Extraction of the fetus by abdominal hysterotomy anytime following a previous cesarean.

D017749.s: The application of industrial management practice to systematically maintain and improve organization-wide performance. Effectiveness and success are determined and assessed by quantitative quality measures.

D019112.s: The electronic transmission of radiological images from one location to another for the purposes of interpretation and/or consultation. Users in different locations may simultaneously view images with greater access to secondary consultations and improved continuing education.

D019167.s: Agents that are used to stimulate appetite. These drugs are frequently used to treat anorexia associated with cancer and AIDS.

D019471.s: The interactions of particles responsible for their scattering and transformations (decays and reactions). Because of interactions, an isolated particle may decay into other particles.

D019545.s: Knowing or understanding without conscious use of reasoning. (Thesaurus of ERIC Descriptors, 1994)

D019804.s: An anti-inflammatory agent, structurally related to the salicylates, which is active in inflammatory bowel disease. It is considered to be the active moiety of sulphasalazine. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed)

D020040.s: The joining of RNA from two different genes. One type of trans-splicing is the spliced leader type (primarily found in protozoans such as trypanosomes and in lower invertebrates such as nematodes) which results in the addition of a capped, noncoding, spliced leader sequence to the 5' end of mRNAs.

D020224.s: Partial cDNA (dna, complementary) sequences that are unique to the cDNAs from which they were derived.

D020493.s: Self-described narratives of a person's life.

D035341.s: A ubiquitously expressed telomere-binding protein that is present at telomeres throughout the cell cycle. It is a suppressor of telomere elongation and may be involved in stabilization of telomere length.

D042361.s: Glandular tissue in the breast of human that is under the influence of hormones such as estrogens; progestins; and prolactin. In women, after parturition, the mammary glands secrete milk (milk, human) for the nourishment of the young.

D042822.s: An increased tendency of the genome to acquire mutations when various processes involved in maintaining and replicating the genome are dysfunctional.

D043762.s: Human behavior or decision related to reproduction.

D050032.s: Transient autoimmune thyroiditis occurring in the postpartum period. It is characterized by the presence of high titers of autoantibodies against thyroid peroxidase and thyroglobulin.

D054403.s: A neoplasm of prolymphocytes affecting the blood, bone marrow, and spleen. It is characterized by prolymphocytes exceeding 55% of the lymphoid cells in the blood and profound splenomegaly.

D055817.s: Delivery of nursing services via remote telecommunications.

D058726.s: Tailored macromolecules harboring covalently-bound biologically active modules that target specific tissues and cells. The active modules or functional groups can include drugs, prodrugs, antibodies, and oligonucleotides, which can act synergistically and be multitargeting.

D061825.s: Types of prosthetic joints in which both wear surfaces of the joint coupling are metallic.

D065821.s: The dorsal region of pons bounded by the middle cerebellar peduncles and the ventral part of the pons. It is continuous with the tegmentum mesencephali and contains cerebellar nuclei, lemnisci and reticular formation.

D000073183.s: A fibrin matrix derived from platelet-rich plasma that contains high concentration of blood platelets; leukocytes; cytokines; and growth factors. It is used in a variety of clinical and tissue engineering applications.

D000073859.s: Functional, psychosocial, emotional and spiritual domains and needs of patients and families following life-threatening disease or events.

D000075602.s: Water pollution from a variety of diffuse sources carried over or through the ground and into water sources such as lakes; rivers; wetlands; coastal waters; and groundwater.

D000077107.s: Determination of the level of functional limitation that may be due to pathology, and evaluating rehabilitative intervention of the way in which the body moves from one point to another. Most often, this is done by walking.

D000080365.s: A form of chorioretinitis characterized by multiple small, cream-colored lesions, symmetrically scattered mainly around the optic disk.

D000090104.s: An image guided examination of the nasolacrimal apparatus including nasolacrimal duct.

D000098427.s: An unsupervised learning network which is composed of two separate networks, a generator which produces content and a discriminator which works to identify real content from the generated content. Over time, generative adversarial networks create data that increasingly resembles the input data.

D000098452.s: Persistent and irrational fear of enclosed places (e.g., elevators, closets, tunnels) or of being confined (e.g., in an airplane or the backseat of a car). Situations where enclosure or confinement may be encountered are often avoided or else endured with intense anxiety or distress.
